newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major wants May 1 poll, sets manifesto themes.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major wants May 1 poll, sets manifesto themes.

text.p: Britain's cabinet decided on Monday that it would aim to hold the election on May 1 and would fight the election on a platform of further strengthening the economy and extending opportunity, ownership and choice to Britons, Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell told reporters.
Dorrell was speaking after a day-long meeting of Prime Minister John Major's cabinet called to draw up the main themes of the ruling Conservative party's manifesto.
Dorrell said the timing of the election was discussed only briefly but added that Major had not changed his view that he wanted to delay it as long as he could.
"We have a five-year mandate and we intend to plan on the basis of completing that mandate," he said.
The election must be held by May 22 but Major has said his preferred date is May 1.
Ministers agreed that if the Conservatives won a fifth consecutive term in office, they would continue with economic and social reforms intended to increase opportunities for all.

"It's a manifesto that will build on 18 years of reform," he said. The minister declined to go into detail about the manifesto but said expanding ownership, choice and opportunity meant, for example, opening more selective grammar schools and improving the National Health Service.
The cabinet also discussed candidates for future privatisation and the next stage of the Conservatives' agenda to deregulate British business. No further details were given.

On economic policy, ministers reaffirmed the twin goal of reducing public spending to less than 40 percent of gross domestic product and moving towards a basic income tax rate of 20 percent, Dorrell said.
They also agreed on the need to ensure that Britain's economy, which they called the strongest in Europe, remained flexible, responsive, deregulated and outward-looking.
The overall aim, he said, was to ensure that "Britain continues to be the best country in the world to live".
